statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk 3% (low) with no Nasdaq-100 price path observable inside the CME weekend halt, against Stress of 79% (high) on an unresolved oil and long-end-yield backdrop.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold, so the mapped policy state stays EA_ON. A narrow danger window is published across the 22:00Z CME reopen and the two hours after it (00:00-03:00 Berlin on 5 October), where the published forecast Tail path reaches the WATCH band on gap and discontinuity risk rather than on observed structure.
headline: Nasdaq-100 carries a record close through the weekend futures halt while an unconfirmed Aramco refinery fire, a Red Sea blockade and a pending OPEC+ decision keep Stress high and Tail at its floor
body:
CME equity-index futures have been halted since Friday 21:00Z and reopen at 22:00Z on 4 October, so no Nasdaq-100 price path exists to assess and Tail stays at its structural floor. The last observed path was orderly two-way behaviour: the index traded to an all-time intraday high of 31,017.53 on Friday 2 October, fully retraced it, and finished at a record 30,807.93 close in the lower part of the session range, up 1.00%, with VIX settling at 15.31, down 6.59%. A record high that is fully retraced into the close is the opposite of the shallow-pullback, repeated-extension structure that Tail measures.

Stress stays high because the backdrop behind that record close is unusually tense and nothing in it resolved over the weekend. Brent is around 102.25 dollars after roughly a 7% monthly gain, and the Federal Reserve H.15 release dated 2 October shows the 2-year at 4.78%, the 5-year at 5.01%, the 10-year at 5.24% and the 30-year at 5.61%. Elevated crude and a 5.24% long-end yield framed the entire prior week.

The Saudi-Houthi escalation remains the dominant unpriced item, and the distinction between claim and confirmation is what keeps it in Stress rather than Tail. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group struck an Aramco facility in Riyadh with ballistic missiles and drones in response to Saudi strikes on Sanaa and other areas it controls; witnesses and news agencies reported flames and black smoke at the site, with emergency crews working to contain the blaze and a perimeter established. The Saudi-led coalition called the Houthi account misleading. As of this assessment neither Saudi authorities nor Aramco have confirmed the cause of the fire, any damage, or any impact on production, refining or exports, and Yemeni government forces are reported to have struck Houthi-controlled Sanaa and Saada in response. The March 2026 Ras Tanura strike, which shut Saudi Arabia's largest domestic refinery for about a week, shows how much an eventual confirmation could matter, but it is precedent rather than evidence about this facility. The durable oil driver remains the Red Sea chokepoint and the declared blockade on Saudi vessels rather than this single unconfirmed fire.

One further checkpoint sits inside the closed session: the OPEC+ monthly production-adjustment group is reported to meet on Sunday 4 October to set next month's targets, with a rollover widely expected. No meeting time was published and no decision had been released at the assessment cutoff, so it is carried as an open checkpoint and not as an event with a verified timestamp. The week ahead is otherwise reported as light, with ISM Services on 5 October and the September FOMC minutes on 7 October the main scheduled catalysts.

The forecast therefore holds Tail between 3% and 6% through the closed Sunday hours, steps it to 12% in the final hour before the reopen, and raises it to 21-23%, inside the WATCH band, across the 22:00Z reopen and the two hours after it. That elevation is gap and discontinuity risk conditional on an unknown first print, not observed structure, and a contained reopen would retire it quickly. The published decay afterwards assumes orderly two-way discovery; a gap that holds without meaningful retracement, a second leg after a failed retracement, or a confirmed Saudi refining outage would each invalidate that assumption. The shared deterministic Finviz context file was stale by several days and only partially collected at assessment time, so it contributed no current evidence and this assessment rests entirely on independently verified primary sources.

lookbackSummary: Across the past 24 published hours Claude held Tail between 5% and 3%, reaching a 3% floor from 12:00Z on 3 October and holding it through the weekend halt, while Stress bottomed at 52% in the European afternoon and then rebuilt steadily to 78% by 08:00Z on 4 October as unpriced weekend escalation accumulated. Confidence stayed in the 83-88% band. Every hour mapped to EA_ON and green, and the dominant mode was normal throughout.
outlookSummary: The closed Sunday session carries no scoreable Nasdaq-100 structure, so Tail is held between 3% and 6% through 20:00Z while Stress sits at a 79% ceiling. Tail then steps to 12% in the final closed hour and is raised to 21-23%, inside the WATCH band, across the 22:00Z CME reopen and the two hours after it, which form the published danger window. It decays conditionally to 10% by 08:00Z on 5 October on the assumption that price discovery is orderly, an assumption that a gap holding without meaningful retracement would invalidate. Confidence troughs at 79% in the final closed hour and recovers to 85% once a continuous path is observable again.
